The most abundant taxa overall, per group, or per sample.

Source: R/taxa_top.r
taxa_top.Rd

taxa_table() with taxa = 5 keeps the five taxa that are most abundant across all samples. taxa_top() ranks the taxa separately within each group of samples (or each sample), so the taxa listed can differ from one group to the next.

Usage

taxa_top(
  biom,
  rank = -1,
  n = 5,
  by = NULL,
  unc = "singly",
  lineage = FALSE,
  transform = "percent"
)

Arguments

biom

An rbiom object, or any value accepted by as_rbiom().

rank

What rank(s) of taxa to display. E.g. "Phylum", "Genus", ".otu", etc. An integer vector can also be given, where 1 is the highest rank, 2 is the second highest, -1 is the lowest rank, -2 is the second lowest, and 0 is the OTU "rank". Run biom$ranks to see all options for a given rbiom object. Default: -1.

n

How many taxa to list for each group. Default: 5

by

Dataset field(s) that define the groups of samples to rank taxa within. Must be categorical. Several fields give one group per combination of their values. Use ".sample" to rank taxa within each sample. NULL ranks taxa across all samples together. Samples with NA in a by field are left out. Default: NULL

unc

How to handle unclassified, uncultured, and similarly ambiguous taxa names. Options are:

"singly" -

Replaces them with the OTU name.

"grouped" -

Replaces them with a higher rank's name.

"drop" -

Excludes them from the result.

"asis" -

To not check/modify any taxa names.

Abbreviations are allowed. Default: "singly"

lineage

Include all ranks in the name of the taxa. For instance, setting to TRUE will produce Bacteria; Actinobacteria; Coriobacteriia; Coriobacteriales. Otherwise the taxa name will simply be Coriobacteriales. You want to set this to TRUE when unc = "asis" and you have taxa names (such as Incertae_Sedis) that map to multiple higher level ranks. Default: FALSE

transform

Units for the abundances in the result. Options are: c("none", "rank", "log", "log1p", "sqrt", "percent"). "percent" gives relative abundances as fractions (0.25 is 25%), and "none" gives counts. See taxa_table() for the others. The choice does not change which taxa are listed. Default: "percent"

Value

A tibble data frame with one row per listed taxon and columns:

.rank

The taxonomic rank.

by field(s)

The group. Not present when by = NULL.

.top

The taxon's position in its group: 1 for the most abundant, up to n.

.taxa

The taxon's name.

.mean

Mean abundance over the group's samples, in transform units.

.prevalence

Fraction of the group's samples in which the taxon was observed.

When by includes ".sample", each group is one sample, and the table has .abundance (in transform units) in place of .mean and .prevalence.

The result carries $code: the R code that regenerates it, including the steps that produced biom.

Details

Taxa are ranked by their mean relative abundance in the group's samples, as taxa_table() ranks them for its taxa argument. Ties are broken alphabetically by taxon name, so the result never depends on a random seed. Taxa that are absent from a group are not listed, so a group can have fewer than n rows.

See also

Other taxa_abundance: sample_sums(), taxa_boxplot(), taxa_clusters(), taxa_corrplot(), taxa_da(), taxa_forest(), taxa_heatmap(), taxa_shared(), taxa_stacked(), taxa_stats(), taxa_sums(), taxa_table(), taxa_upset()

Examples

    library(rbiom)

    biom <- rarefy(hmp50)

    # The five most abundant genera overall.
    taxa_top(biom)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   .rank  .top .taxa              .mean .prevalence
#>   <fct> <int> <fct>              <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 Genus     1 Lactobacillus     0.181        0.286
#> 2 Genus     2 Streptococcus     0.168        0.714
#> 3 Genus     3 Bacteroides       0.0956       0.449
#> 4 Genus     4 Corynebacterium 1 0.0836       0.245
#> 5 Genus     5 Haemophilus       0.0474       0.551

    # The three most abundant phyla at each body site.
    taxa_top(biom, rank = "Phylum", n = 3, by = "Body Site")
#> # A tibble: 15 × 6
#>    .rank  `Body Site`     .top .taxa            .mean .prevalence
#>    <fct>  <fct>          <int> <fct>            <dbl>       <dbl>
#>  1 Phylum Anterior nares     1 Actinobacteria 0.657         1    
#>  2 Phylum Anterior nares     2 Firmicutes     0.270         1    
#>  3 Phylum Anterior nares     3 Proteobacteria 0.0540        0.8  
#>  4 Phylum Buccal mucosa      1 Firmicutes     0.788         1    
#>  5 Phylum Buccal mucosa      2 Proteobacteria 0.125         1    
#>  6 Phylum Buccal mucosa      3 Bacteroidetes  0.0554        1    
#>  7 Phylum Mid vagina         1 Firmicutes     0.974         1    
#>  8 Phylum Mid vagina         2 Bacteroidetes  0.0107        0.8  
#>  9 Phylum Mid vagina         3 Actinobacteria 0.00668       0.8  
#> 10 Phylum Saliva             1 Firmicutes     0.446         1    
#> 11 Phylum Saliva             2 Proteobacteria 0.261         1    
#> 12 Phylum Saliva             3 Bacteroidetes  0.181         1    
#> 13 Phylum Stool              1 Bacteroidetes  0.669         1    
#> 14 Phylum Stool              2 Firmicutes     0.287         1    
#> 15 Phylum Stool              3 Proteobacteria 0.0299        0.889

    # The dominant genus in each sample.
    taxa_top(biom, n = 1, by = ".sample")
#> # A tibble: 49 × 5
#>    .rank .sample  .top .taxa             .abundance
#>    <fct> <fct>   <int> <fct>                  <dbl>
#>  1 Genus HMP01       1 Streptococcus          0.657
#>  2 Genus HMP02       1 Streptococcus          0.461
#>  3 Genus HMP03       1 Streptococcus          0.249
#>  4 Genus HMP04       1 Fusobacterium          0.133
#>  5 Genus HMP05       1 Streptococcus          0.683
#>  6 Genus HMP06       1 Haemophilus            0.205
#>  7 Genus HMP07       1 Streptococcus          0.761
#>  8 Genus HMP08       1 Haemophilus            0.347
#>  9 Genus HMP09       1 Haemophilus            0.142
#> 10 Genus HMP10       1 Corynebacterium 1      0.440
#> # ℹ 39 more rows
